rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so headroom exists to raise obfuscation intensity. SUB stays near-maximal since arithmetic substitution is cheap and effective on RC4's byte-manipulation-heavy code (rc4_setup/rc4_crypt rely on modular add and XOR), with low risk of changing semantics. SPLIT and IGV are boosted as low-cost structure diversifiers that break basic-block and global-variable recognizability with negligible runtime impact on this 166-line program. ICALL is kept high to hide the rc4_setup/rc4_crypt call edges behind indirect dispatch — correctness risk is modest now that round 1 validated the toolchain (no ICE fallback) — but capped below 1 because indirect calls in rc4_crypt's tight loop add real per-iteration cost. BCF and FLA are raised moderately rather than maximally: rc4_crypt is an extremely hot inner loop (78 bytes, per-byte keystream work), so aggressive bogus control flow and flattening there would inflate runtime beyond acceptable bounds; moderate weights let the feature-driven selector apply them to the colder main/rc4_setup while restraining them on the hot loop. IBR is raised to interpose opaque jumps between blocks, cheap relative to its disruption of static CFG recovery. All passes remain enabled for maximum diversity; no pass is disabled since correctness held at round 1.
